title: Smallest Rotation with Highest Score
statement:
Rotating `nums` by `k` (where `0 <= k < nums.length`) moves the first `k` values to the back in their original order, so the array reads `nums[k], ..., nums[n - 1], nums[0], ..., nums[k - 1]`. In the rotated array, every position `j` whose value is at most `j` earns one point, and the score of `k` is the total of those points.

Return the `k` with the largest score. When several values of `k` reach that score, return the smallest of them.
notes:
## Intuition

Scoring every rotation directly costs O(n²). Instead, look at one value at a time. After rotating by `k`, the value at index `i` lands at position `(i - k + n) % n`, and it earns a point when that position is at least `nums[i]`. The good positions `nums[i]`, ..., `n - 1` correspond to a run of consecutive `k` values (possibly wrapping past the end), so each value adds +1 to one cyclic range of rotations. A difference array records all those ranges in O(1) each, and one prefix sum turns it into the score of every `k`.

## Approach

1. Make `diff` of length `n + 1`, all zero.
2. For index `i`, the rotations that score it run from `start = (i + 1) % n` (it lands at `n - 1`) to `end = (i - nums[i] + n) % n` (it lands at `nums[i]`).
3. If `start <= end`, add +1 at `start` and -1 at `end + 1`. Otherwise the range wraps, so mark `[0, end]` and `[start, n - 1]` separately.
4. Sweep `k` from 0 upward, adding `diff[k]` into `score`. Update `best` only on a strictly larger score so the smallest `k` wins ties.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 3, 1, 4, 0]`, `n = 5`. The ranges are: `i = 0`: `[1, 3]`; `i = 1`: `[2, 3]`; `i = 2`: wraps, `[3, 4]` and `[0, 1]`; `i = 3`: `[4, 4]`; `i = 4`: `[0, 4]`. So `diff = [2, 1, 0, 1, -1, -3]`. The running `score` is 2, 3, 3, 4, 3 for `k = 0..4`. The first strict maximum is 4 at `k = 3`, so the answer is `3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index marks at most two ranges, then one sweep.
- Space: O(n) for `diff`.

## Pitfalls

- The range of good rotations can wrap around the end; splitting it into two pieces is required.
- A value of 0 scores in every rotation; its range covers all `n` values of `k`.
- Use `>` (not `>=`) when updating `best`, or a later tie would replace the smallest `k`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `nums` |
| `diff` | difference array over rotations `k` |
| `start`, `end` | first and last rotation (cyclically) where `nums[i]` scores |
| `score` | running prefix sum: the score of rotation `k` |
| `bestScore`, `best` | highest score so far and its smallest `k` |
